about: Full Spectrum's versions and what each brought, as Solar Timeline does it. One definition: the header's version, the What's new panel (js/whatsnew.js) and the landing page read this. A release is 'released' or 'next'. GitHub Pages publishes main as it is, so a 'next' release shows only away from the live site; date it and set it 'released' when it ships, and make package.json's version match (tests/releases.mjs). An item's `go`: an address in the app, opened by Show me. `kind`: new, better or fix.

items.text: Jupiter, Neptune, the Earth and the Moon wear real maps made from NASA data (Solar System Scope); the Earth has its clouds, a sheen on the sea and city lights on its night side
Everest is built from real heights, a block of ground from sea level to the summit with Lhotse and Nuptse beside it, snow and glacier where they lie
The Burj Khalifa is built from its real plan: three wings round a core, stepping back one at a time in a spiral to the spire
The wave view says what the wave's height means: not a size but the strength of the electric field, set by brightness rather than wavelength (about 870 volts per metre in full sunlight)

releases.title: Real molecules, and into Solar Timeline

items.text: Links into Solar Timeline: fly round the Sun from the sky view and from Hot things, and round Jupiter, Neptune, the Earth and the Moon from the wave view
The proton is Molecule Viewer's: three quarks trading colour, the gluon strings between them, and a sea of quark-antiquark pairs flickering in and out

Much better small things: haemoglobin, DNA and the ribosome are built atom by atom or residue by residue from their real structures in the Protein Data Bank; the flu virus is studded with real copies of its two spike proteins and cut open to show its genome; the giant virus and the bacterium are cut open too

The red blood cell is cut open to show it packed with haemoglobin; the water molecule sits in the cloud of its ten electrons, gathered to the oxygen; the hydrogen atom's cloud shimmers and the uranium nucleus is packed, both as Molecule Viewer draws them
Photons: cards under the beam with what one photon carries and can do, how many a beam holds each second, the push of light, and, for visible light, how few your eye can see
Hot things: the examples are a row of pictures under the chart, from the cosmic microwave background to the Sun's corona, each with its temperature and the colour it glows, credited
Fields in 3D could come up blank after the tour, or after quick clicks, with only the labels showing
The 3D model's credit no longer shows over Fields in 3D

releases.title: The whole spectrum, end to end

items.text: One dial from radio to gamma rays, 3 Hz to 12 PeV, with the wavelength, frequency and photon energy at the cursor; type any of them to jump there, and every place has its own address
Forty real things at their wavelengths, from the Schumann resonance to the most energetic photon ever seen, each with what makes it and what it does
The wave at a scale you can feel: the light at the cursor beside a 3D model of something the same size, from Jupiter to a proton
Light as electric and magnetic fields in 3D, linear or circular, labelled, with how strong they are in sunlight; or as photons, counted in a beam (Wave, Fields in 3D and Photons, under the picture)

Visible light up close: a prism ray-traced through real glass, the lines of five elements against the dark lines in sunlight, the Sun's spectrum above and below the air, and how people and other animals see colour
Hot things: why everything glows, from the cosmic microwave background to the Sun's corona, and where each one's power goes
Through the air: what reaches the ground across the spectrum, what absorbs the rest, and twelve telescopes, on mountains or in space and why
The sky in every light: the Milky Way, the Sun and the Crab Nebula in radio, infrared, visible, X-rays and gamma rays, each picture explained
A guided journey from the longest waves to the shortest, a tour of every view, Surprise me, sound, and a picture to save
What's new, here, and a way to send feedback
